title: Signal-to-SLA Mapping & Intake Playbook for Hosted Chat/Toolcall Requests
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background: Enterprise customers increasingly submit multi-dimensional feature requests against the hosted API (chat + streaming + tool/function calling + structured outputs). Current intake often forces manual judgement calls and inconsistent SLA/priority assignments; this leads to missed commitments, unclear resourcing, and difficulty routing to Dedicated/Private sales or engineering tracks.

Problem Statement: We need a repeatable, evidence-driven playbook to convert incoming customer signals (usage, contract SLAs, regulatory needs, cost impact, security posture) into prioritized intake lanes with explicit SLO/SLA recommendations and routing (self-serve, enterprise backlog, Dedicated sales, Private deployment). The playbook must cover quick-decision rules for streaming/toolcalls and structured-output requests that have operational impacts (e.g., real-time latency SLOs, data residency, KMS requirements).

Scope: This ticket covers the PM-owned intake playbook, decision matrix, and automation knobs for the Hosted API request triage. Includes: decision tree for priority buckets, required signal surface for submissions, templated customer intake form, routing rules to engineering/Dedicated/Private, and acceptance criteria for automated priority classification. Out of scope: implementation of the full automation pipeline and console UI (separate eng tickets).

Goals:
- Reduce median manual triage time from 36h to <6h for enterprise-hosted feature requests.
- Surface a deterministic SLA bucket and routing recommendation for >=85% of incoming enterprise requests.
- Provide clear escalation rules for requests that impact latency, cost, or data residency.

Non-functional requirements:
- Playbook must be auditable (decision logs preserved in ticket comments).
- Must be conservative on security/regulatory flags (default to escalate to Private/Dedicated reviews).
- Easy for Sales/CS to use during customer conversations (single-page checklist + 3-minute form).
acceptance_criteria: A one-page decision matrix that maps input signals to priority buckets exists and is reviewed by Eng + Security.
A templated intake form (Google Form + internal shortcut) collects required signals for automated classification.
Routing rules that recommend one of: Self-serve backlog, Hosted-feature P2/P1, Dedicated sales funnel, Private deployment review are defined and documented.
Pilot classification accuracy >= 85% on a historical sample of 200 recent enterprise requests.
Escalation play (who to call and expected SLAs) defined for high-risk flags: latency <100ms target, customer data residency/GDPR, required KMS/HSM, HIPAA/regulated workloads.
proposed_solution:
Phase 1 (PM-led) produce the decision matrix and templated intake form. Use historical request data (customer emails, support tickets, and prior Linear tickets) to derive signal weights. Phase 2 (pilot) run the playbook against a 2-week live stream of inbound enterprise requests and measure alignment vs manual triage. Phase 3 (hand-off) create eng tickets to implement automated classifier and Console UI for routing recommendations.

Key decision heuristics proposed: weight contract SLA and scale signal highest for prioritization; treat any explicit data residency/KMS/regulatory requirement as automatic Private/Dedicated review; treat streaming with sub-250ms latency requirement as "low-latency" bucket that triggers runtime perf eng review.

Artifacts to produce: one-page decision matrix (Confluence), templated intake form (Google Drive), sample dataset for pilot (CSV of 200 past requests), short training doc for Sales/CS (1 pager).
metrics: % of requests auto-routed to correct lane
Number of escalations to Private/Dedicated due to misclassification
rollout_plan: Week 1: Draft decision matrix and intake form; review with Eng, Security, Sales.
Week 2: Refine weights using historical data; generate pilot dataset and evaluation scripts.
Week 3: Run 2-week pilot on live requests; collect feedback and error cases.
Week 4: Finalize playbook; prepare hand-off package for automation (eng tickets + acceptance criteria).
Post-release: Quarterly review of signal weights and false-positive/negative audit.
open_questions: What threshold of customer ARR or committed spend should immediately mark a request as P0/P1?
Do we require Sales/CS sign-off before a request can be routed to Dedicated/Private lanes?
Which data source is canonical for historical severity (Zendesk vs Linear vs Sales notes)?
Should runtime perf constraints be captured as numerical fields on intake (e.g., target p95 latency)?
